properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): export_graph's path-mode RECEIPT has echoed the document's whole stamp since 2026-07-20, when the stamp was four small fields. The stamp then grew type-name lists (07-24) and every enum set (09-12) for the IMPORT guard, a different reader, so the receipt is now 8,035 chars, 96% stamp. The reply-bound gate exempts export_graph by TOOL name as "the design document itself", which is true only of the no-path mode, so the receipt was never measured
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-09-28, triaging art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-09-28 (hxm_program hub, 2026-09-25, reflow2 0.69.0 → 0.70.0) under rule:field-feedback-issues-are-root-caused-and-ideas-are-brainstormed.

① OBSERVED, the reporter's words: "F-28 — every `export_graph` reply carries the whole schema stamp (all edge-type names and every enum value set, ~6 KB), once per commit, many commits per session. It adds nothing a caller acts on; `budget_chars` is not accepted there ("unknown field"). A `stamp_summary` (version + counts) by default would do." EXPECTED: a receipt for a write to `path` carries what the caller acts on: where it landed, whether it wrote, the lineage, and which reflow2 wrote it. NOT AFFECTED: the exported FILE, whose stamp is load-bearing for import.

② PRECEDENT (searched on the reporter's words): cap:every-oversized-reply-offers-a-bound and fact:the-reply-budget-sweep-is-built-2026-09-13, which lists export_graph as "document_exempt" ("export_graph stays excluded for the same reason" as get_instructions and export_surface). fact:defect-export-graph-stamps-confidently-while-the-server-reports-itself-stale is about the stamp's correctness, not its size. There is no prior record of the receipt's size.

③ CANDIDATES:
(A) CHANGE. The receipt copied the stamp when it was small, and the stamp later grew for another reader. Nobody re-read the receipt.
(B) ASSURANCE. The only size check exempts the tool by name, and it also sweeps only no-argument calls, so a path-mode reply is never measured.
(C) CONTRACT. Something downstream needs the full stamp in the receipt, so trimming it would break a consumer.
(D) CONTENT POLICY. The client receives the payload twice (duplicate policy), inflating what the reporter saw.
(E) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG. The reporter called without `path` and saw the document, not a receipt.

④ WHAT WOULD SEPARATE THEM: the receipt's composition and the stamp's history test (A). The gate's exemption list tests (B). A search for consumers of receipt["stamp"] tests (C). The size of the text block tests (D). The reporter's own description ("once per commit") tests (E).

⑤ RESULTS (0.74.0 binary, scratch store of 5 nodes; source at 70e547f):
· The receipt is 8,035 chars. `stamp` is 7,681 of them: enum_values 6,222, edge_type_names 915, node_type_names 399, the rest counts and versions. The stamp's size does not depend on the design's size. The other nine receipt keys (path, bytes, nodes, edges, content_hash, prev_content_hash, chained_from, wrote, taken_at) total about 350.
· History: exchange.rs line 215 has put `"stamp": export.stamp` in the receipt since 939f342 (2026-07-20, BL-48/49), when GraphStamp was reflow2_version, schema_version, node_types and edge_types. b660df5 (2026-07-24, BL-86) added the type-name lists. e58f7b2 (2026-09-12, #486, "A vocabulary change is never silent") added enum_values for the IMPORT guard. Each addition had a reader in the FILE; none was made for the receipt.
· tools/replies_are_bounded.py DOCUMENT_SHAPED: "export_graph": "returns the design document itself". That holds without `path`; with `path` the reply is a receipt. The gate also calls only no-argument tools.
· Consumers of the receipt's stamp: tools/export_via_binary.py reads sc['stamp']['reflow2_version'], only the version. smoke_mcp.py and tests/tools.rs read the DOCUMENT's stamp, not the receipt's.
· `budget_chars`: "unknown field `budget_chars`, expected one of `path`, `overwrite`, `accept_divergence`". The tool takes three parameters.
· The content text block under the signpost policy is 1,242 chars, so (D) does not explain it. Only one reply in the whole MCP crate echoes a stamp.
⇒ (A) and (B) HOLD. (C) REFUTED: the one consumer reads only the version. (D) REFUTED under the default policy. (E) REFUTED: a receipt is the only reply "once per commit" fits, and it carries the stamp by construction.

⑥ CLASS: a field copied BY REFERENCE into a reply grows with its source, for a reader the reply does not have, and the exemption that would have caught it was granted per TOOL rather than per reply shape. Would a fix at the class have stopped earlier reports? The reply-budget sweep of 2026-09-13 measured reply shapes one tool at a time. A per-shape exemption, or a receipt that names its fields, would have kept the receipt at about 350 chars through all three stamp changes. Narrow recurrence: DOCUMENT_SHAPED has 3 entries. get_instructions and export_surface have second shapes too (section, and a path-mode receipt), but neither echoes a growing field.

⑦ OUT OF SCOPE (no code changed). A test pinning the class: call export_graph with `path` and assert the receipt carries reflow2_version and schema_version (plus counts) and no name lists or enum sets. Assert it stays under a fixed small size as the schema grows, for example by seeding extra enum values. The bounded-replies gate would list reply SHAPES (export_graph:path is a receipt, export_graph:no-path a document) rather than tools.

REPORTER'S CONCLUSIONS: HELD. "adds nothing a caller acts on" is true for every field but reflow2_version. "budget_chars not accepted": true, and it is the wrong lever anyway, because the receipt is not over any budget; it is noise repeated per commit. PROPOSED FIX (the reporter's): the receipt carries a stamp summary (reflow2_version, schema_version, node_types, edge_types) and says the full stamp is in the file.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: the reporter's ~6 KB against the measured 7.7 KB on 0.74.0 is consistent with enum sets that have grown since 0.70.0, but was not measured on 0.70.0. Nor was how the reporter's harness counts a reply (structuredContent or text).
